Goal operations are covered by the Go goal handle, app-server routing, and router envelope tests that prove logical continuations coalesce across physical turns and regular turns stay blocked while a goal is active.
Go normalizes typed app-server inputs, including data-URL images, and validates the resulting turn-start payload through the public client.
Go preserves local-image compatibility input handling and also validates the typed app-server local-image payload shape.
Go preserves typed skill inputs in app-server payload normalization and validates full mixed-input turn-start payload construction through the public client.
Go validates name mutation and thread readback through the context-first client and thread wrappers.
Go validates initialize metadata capture at the transport layer and exposes it through the public Client surface.
Go validates thread-list request parameter mapping, including the archived filter, on the public client surface.
Go validates typed thread-read decoding, including persisted turns and goal state, on the rebuilt thread record surface.
Go uses one concurrency-safe client API instead of separate async wrappers, so the same lifecycle wrappers cover concurrent callers.
Go validates forked-thread lifecycle wrappers and the distinct returned thread id.
Go validates archive and unarchive lifecycle wrappers against the app-server transport.
Go validates model-list RPCs through the context-first Client surface.
Go validates thread compaction through both the public wrapper and the client lifecycle surface.
Go validates API-key, browser, and device-code login flows plus follow-up account/model access on the rebuilt public client surfaces.
Go validates API-key, browser, and device-code login flows plus follow-up account/model access on the rebuilt public client surfaces.
Go validates completed-turn aggregation, usage extraction, and final-response collection through both compatibility and rebuilt client paths.
Go validates turn-start payload mapping for model/cwd/reasoning/output-schema inputs and usage extraction on the public client surface.
Go uses one concurrency-safe API surface instead of separate async wrappers, so the same run aggregation tests plus the direct concurrent-request correlation test cover the Python async duplicate.
Go validates final-response extraction from collected turn items on the compatibility run path that feeds the rebuilt result surface.
Go keeps final-response extraction tied to the collected assistant item rather than inventing extra text, matching the result-selection contract.
Go keeps final-response selection bound to explicit assistant/final-answer items instead of promoting commentary-only notifications.

Go validates the unknown-phase final-response fallback directly on the rebuilt client and separately proves the same transport/client surface remains correct under heavy concurrent request correlation.
Go validates commentary-only runs do not synthesize a final response and separately proves the same transport/client surface remains correct under heavy concurrent request correlation.
Go validates failed-turn propagation to the caller as a stable returned error.
Go validates agent-message phase decoding and final-response preservation across transport/event mapping.
Go validates streamed turn lifecycle events on the public client path and router replay of early notifications into the registered turn stream.
Go validates both streaming and collected-turn completion paths against the same completed-turn result contract.
Go exposes one concurrency-safe streaming API, so the same stream contract plus the direct concurrent-request correlation test cover the Python async duplicate.
Go validates router delivery and replay semantics on registered turn streams, including cancellation not consuming queued events.
Go directly validates model listing while a turn stream remains open and separately proves the client transport correlates a large number of concurrent in-flight requests.
Go validates turn-routing envelopes are keyed by turn id and remain isolated from goal/global routing.
Go validates turn-routing envelopes are keyed by turn id, remain isolated from goal routing, and continue to correlate correctly under heavy concurrent request traffic.
Go validates steer and interrupt controls on the context-first turn handle surface.

Go exposes a single goroutine-safe client instead of Python async wrappers, and directly proves concurrent transport correlation with one thousand shuffled in-flight responses.
Go has no separate async wrapper layer, so the public turn-handle wrappers and router replay tests cover the same notification registration/delegation contract on the single client implementation.
Go uses generated alias-aware struct tags rather than Python snake_case Pydantic fields, and validates the marshaled wire aliases directly.
Go validates the generated type set against the schema bundle so shared definitions are emitted once and stay in sync.
Go keeps future enum values typed through generated string-backed enums, covering newer runtime plan values.
Go keeps known and future enum values typed through generated string-backed enums used by public request structs.
Go preserves thread-source wire aliases and future string values through generated request structs and enums.
Go preserves the auto-review approval reviewer value through generated/public approval settings and typed decoding.
Go validates canonical notification method inference and typed decoding helpers on the rebuilt protocol surface.
Go validates unknown notifications fall back to raw/unknown union payloads without losing bytes.
Go validates malformed known notifications fail closed into raw fallback payloads.
Go validates turn-id extraction across direct, nested, and unscoped notification payload shapes.
Go validates registered turn routes receive the matching envelopes keyed by turn id.
Go validates goal operation routing by thread id while preserving mirrored turn envelopes.
Go validates per-turn queued routing/replay semantics on the shared router used by the client reader loop.
Go validates early turn events are replayed once the turn registers.
Go validates completed/unregistered routes do not leave stale pending state behind.
Go preserves unknown notification routing by falling back to raw payloads and extracting turn ids when present.
Go runs an explicit generator drift verifier against the checked-in protocol artifacts.
Go validates initialize/start failures surface as transport errors and closes the client on failed startup paths.
Go validates failed initialization closes and reaps the underlying child transport directly on the rebuilt client startup path.

Go initializes eagerly in NewClient, then validates concurrent public operations reuse that initialized transport without issuing another initialize request; the captured initialize count remains exactly one.
Go validates high-level approval presets serialize to the expected app-server approval policy and reviewer fields.
Go restricts approval presets to the supported discoverable enum values and validates the translation helper directly.
Go validates sandbox preset serialization on app-server thread and turn payloads.
Go exposes typed sandbox modes on the public API rather than raw ad-hoc strings, and rejects invalid configuration inputs during argument normalization.
Go keeps retry helpers and example/fixture code on typed status and error helpers rather than ad-hoc string comparisons.
Go publishes the configuration type through the stable exported package API, verified by the public API snapshot.
Go exposes the collected TurnResult type and validates its observed fields on the context-first path.
Go verifies the exported run methods remain part of the compile-time public API contract.
Go compile fixtures prove the public run/turn helpers accept the documented shorthand inputs on the exported API surface.
Go exposes typed approval presets and validates their public translation behavior.
Go exposes typed sandbox presets on the public API and validates their serialized wire form.
Python package-version self-reporting is wheel metadata specific; the Go module publishes versioned tags/releases instead of an import-time package version constant.
Go validates the exported package/help surface through `go doc -all` snapshot coverage instead of Python `help()` docstrings.
`py.typed` is a Python packaging marker with no Go module equivalent.
Python `__all__` export curation is language-specific; Go exposes only capitalized package exports and validates them through the public API snapshot.
Star-import behavior is Python-specific; Go relies on package exports validated by the public API snapshot.
Python type-module export curation is language-specific; Go publishes generated protocol types directly in the protocol package and verifies schema coverage.
Python type-module star-import behavior is language-specific; Go publishes generated protocol types directly in the protocol package and verifies schema coverage.
Go compile fixtures and examples validate that documented consumers use only the supported public package surface.
Python keyword-only snake_case signatures are language-specific; Go validates the stable typed public API through exported signatures and compile fixtures.
Go validates the typed approval preset defaults used for new thread work.
Go validates resumed/forked/existing thread operations preserve stored approval settings unless explicitly overridden.
Go validates lifecycle methods are exposed on the client/thread surfaces documented by the exported public API.
Go validates initialize metadata parsing and exposure of protocol/server identity through the rebuilt client.
Go fails closed when initialize metadata is malformed or missing required identity information.
